sentences.text: Manik Ruhidas & Ors vs Unknown on 18 May, 2016

Author: Joymalya Bagchi
Bench: Joymalya Bagchi
93. 18.05.2016 C.R.R. 1644 of 2016 Aloke Ct. No.28 In the matter of : Manik Ruhidas & Ors.
Mr. Sujan Chatterjee ... for the petitioner s Proceeding in the instant case being S.C. Case No. 137
(12) of 2015 pending before learned Sessions Judge, 3rd Court, Tamluk, Purba Medinipur arising
out of Moyna P.S. Case No. 228 of 2015 under Sections 272/273 Ipc and Section 304/120B Ipc and
Section 46Aa of the Bengal Excise Act and Section 16(3) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act
has been challenged.

Mr. Chatterjee, learned counsel for the petitioners submits that the offence under Section 46AA of the Bengal Excise Act and Section 16(3) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act are triable by the learned Magistrate and, therefore, proceeding before the Court of Sessions is not maintainable.
I am unable to accept such contention.
The allegations in the instant case relate to sale of spurious liquor by the petitioners resulting in death of large number of persons.
Prima facie, the allegations disclose the ingredients of the offences punishable under Section 304 of the IPC as well as Sections 272/273 of the IPC.

Such offences are triable by the Court of Sessions and, accordingly, the institution and continuation of the proceeding before the Court of the Additional Sessions Judge, 3rd Court, Tamluk, Purba Medinipure cannot be said to be illegal or without jurisdiction.
